quotes.text: Stripe handles the logic for dynamically displaying the most relevant eligible payment methods to each customer.

| [Affirm](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/affirm.md) | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported 1,2 | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | - Unsupported | ✓ Supported | - Unsupported | ✓ Supported 4 | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |

| [Klarna](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna.md) | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported 5 | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported3 | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported 4 | - Unsupported | (Private preview) |

1 Not supported when using Checkout in subscription mode.2 Not supported when using Checkout in setup mode.3 Not supported when saving payment details during payment (`setup_future_usage`).4 Only supports the [send_invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/object.md#invoice_object-collection_method) collection method.5 Availability varies by buyer country and Klarna payment option.

findings: Both captures define BNPL as provider-managed customer installments with the merchant paid immediately and in full; the customer chooses a provider, signs in, accepts or declines repayment terms, then returns to merchant site. Dynamic payment methods are enabled by default and configured in Dashboard for eligible customer display across Checkout/hosted/embedded/Elements/invoice routes; manual listing requires method-specific guides. Provider selection or browser return is not proof of approved financing or payment success. New raw/stripe-payments-buy-now-pay-later-2026-11-07.md:9-38; old raw/stripe-bnpl-overview-2025.md:8-36; current wiki/sources/source-stripe-bnpl-overview.md:13-19 focuses matrices and misses the eligibility/state boundary.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/buy-now-pay-later, Stripe describes BNPL as provider-managed installments: the merchant is described as paid immediately in full, while the buyer selects a service, signs in, accepts or declines repayment terms and returns to the merchant. Dynamic methods are enabled by default and Dashboard-configurable, then displayed to eligible buyers in Checkout or related UI paths; a return is not payment success. New raw lines 9-38 and 39-95 provide product, API and transaction matrices with method-specific limits. Old raw lines 8-36 and 38-95 provide the matched baseline. The November matrix changes Affirm Subscriptions to unsupported and Customer Portal to supported; Klarna Terminal to private preview and Checkout to country/option-dependent; Mondu/Scalapay/SeQura mobile support, SeQura send_invoice Invoicing, and SeQura setup_future_usage to unsupported. source-stripe-bnpl-overview.md lines 13-33 is now stale on Affirm and SeQura, omitted Sunbit's already-supported setup_future_usage, and overstates the ten-row API matrix as all eleven methods.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/buy-now-pay-later, substantive changes are support-cell and footnote changes, especially Affirm subscription/portal, Klarna Checkout/Terminal, three mobile rows, SeQura Invoicing and future-use (new raw lines 41-72 versus old raw lines 40-71). The Elements quickstart link, list numbering, table whitespace and line-wrapped transaction rows are presentation/navigation. Historical May support cells stay dated; missing Klarna send_invoice footnote does not by itself prove automatic collection. source-stripe-bnpl-overview.md and the BNPL concept need reciprocal warnings: November SeQura future-use conflicts with May, Sunbit was omitted at baseline, and both overview Connect tables conflict with dated method-specific Kriya/Mondu/SeQura/Scalapay Connect-No captures. The API matrix omits Scalapay, so this overview alone cannot guarantee its PaymentIntent/redirect behavior. Buyer eligibility, provider approval, successful payment and payout remain distinct from dynamic display and browser return.
